purpose: Routes that have been closed, with the reason each fails. A proposal that matches a closed lane must either cite new information that defeats the stated obstruction, or be rejected without spending a Lean build on it.

closure_kinds.circular: an exact identity that restates the target in other notation; proving it is proving the target
closure_kinds.lossy: the route is sound but discards more than the target can afford
closure_kinds.ceiling: the mechanism is real but its best case is provably weaker than the target

lanes.title: Bound the wheel residual by summing separately bounded square blocks
lanes.claim: Per-block bounds on Delta_j, summed, control the pinned wheel residual R_k.
lanes.obstruction: Only the signed sum telescopes. sum_{j<=J} Delta_j = R_k(X_J) - R_k(X_0), so replacing it by sum_j |Delta_j| discards exactly the cancellation being sought. Measured loss over mu-sieved data: 29.7x at J=64, 660x at J=256, 67.5x at J=1024, against sqrt(J) = 8.0, 16.0, 32.0. Over a full primorial block J is astronomically larger.

evidence.lean_note: The module header states this directly: an absolute-value sum over the blocks loses a full square-root factor.

lanes.what_would_reopen: A bound on the SIGNED consecutive sums that does not pass through per-block absolute values. Note that such a bound is the wheel residual bound itself, so this is circular unless it supplies independent correlation information about adjacent Delta_j.

lanes.title: Differentiate the square-root smooth/transport prefix decomposition
lanes.claim: Differencing M(X_n) = A_n - T_n exposes a new cross-n cancellation mechanism.
lanes.obstruction: The decomposition is at the PREFIX level (squarePrefixMertens_eq_squareRootSmooth_sub_transport), so the increment is Delta A_n - Delta T_n. The reclassification term created when the square-root cutoff advances appears in both increments with the same sign and cancels identically, returning Delta A_n - Delta T_n = Delta_n. The derivative removes the moving-cutoff mechanism rather than exposing it.
lanes.what_would_reopen: Nothing at the level of the raw (A,T) pair. The lifetime decomposition M(X_t) = L + Z + D is the productive replacement, since it discharges two of three terms unconditionally.

lanes.title: Bound the survivor via residue energy and finite Cauchy-Schwarz
lanes.claim: |Z|^2 <= s (D + C) with negative cross-cofactor covariance C cancelling the diagonal D delivers an RH-scale survivor bound for some modulus schedule.
lanes.obstruction: C is indeed negative at every modulus tested, but the fibre split and the prime-face toggle are governed by the same object: the square-unit subgroup mod s. For s | 24 every unit has q^2 = 1, so u = const - c^2 is a FUNCTION of c, the split is Z re-bucketed, and proving the energy small is proving the survivor bound. Raising s makes the fibres informative (30.6 fibres per cofactor at s=10080) but degrades V/D from 1e-4 to 0.61 while the factor s enters the bound. At t=600, |Z| = 27 against a target of t = 600, yet sqrt(sV) never falls below 1642 at any modulus tested.
lanes.caveats: t <= 600 (X_t ~ 3.6e5) is small and sqrt(sV)/t IS falling with t at s=12 (4.68 -> 2.74 across t=200..600). The closure is on the STRUCTURE - degeneracy trades against the Cauchy factor - not on the numerics alone.
lanes.what_would_reopen: Applying the toggle pairing BEFORE passing to residues: cancel matched (c, c*ell) sources directly in Z = sum_c -mu(c) K(c), leaving the boundary set {c : c*ell*q > X_t} as the unpaired remainder. That keeps the mechanism and never introduces s, so neither the degeneracy nor the Cauchy factor applies.
lanes.reopener_outcome: Tried on 2026-08-09 and carried out; it terminates in the lane 'canonical-orientation-split' below. Pairing before residues is exactly the far-upper survivor route, and RHLean/Proof/SurvivorFarUpperRigidity.lean proves the fixed-q fibre is then the FULL negative reciprocal Mertens prefix -M(floor(X_t/q)) with no unpaired-boundary saving at all. The remainder set {c : c*ell*q > X_t} is empty in the far range, so the pairing cancels nothing there.

lanes.title: Split the square-root smooth mass by canonical orientation (c < q against q <= c) and bound the matched born-smooth / transport object
lanes.claim: squareRootMatchedBornSmoothTransport R = bornSmooth R - transport R is the residual carrying the large cancellation, so an RH-scale bound on it (equivalently on bornSmooth + farUpperSurvivor, which differs from it by the elementary 7R root strip) delivers the RH-scale Mertens bound.
lanes.obstruction: The orientation split leaves exactly one region uncancelled, and that region is a pi-weighted Mertens sum of true order R^(3/2)/log R, a full quarter power of X = R^2-1 above the X^(1/2+eps) target. Writing q = P+(m) and c = m/q, the positive-orientation region c < q <= R collapses in closed form to squareRootPositiveSmoothMass R = -sum_{q<=R prime} M(q-1) = -sum_{c<R} mu(c)*(pi(R)-pi(c)), and M(R^2-1) = positiveSmooth R + matched R. Summation by parts turns positiveSmooth into an INTEGRAL of M against dpi: integration is a smoothing that removes precisely the sign oscillation the target needs. Under RH the explicit formula gives int_1^R M(t)dt = sum_rho R^(rho+1)/(rho(rho+1)zeta'(rho)) + O(1), every term of modulus exactly R^(3/2)/|rho(rho+1)zeta'(rho)|, so no cancellation among zeros can push it below R^(3/2-o(1)). Hence matched R = M(R^2-1) - positiveSmooth R is itself of order R^(3/2)/log R. The route is self-defeating: if |matched| << R^(1+eps) were proved, then |M(R^2-1)| >= |positiveSmooth| - |matched| would be Omega(R^(3/2-eps)) = Omega(X^(3/4-eps)), which DISPROVES RH.

measured.normalised_band: |positiveSmooth| * log R / R^1.5 stays in [0.0079, 0.0202] for R in [1e5, 5.37e8] - flat over four decades
measured.ratio_to_R: |positiveSmooth|/R rises from 0.32 at R=128 to 18.96 at R=5.37e8, i.e. it diverges away from the R^(1+eps) target
measured.mechanism_check: positiveSmooth R / (-int_2^R M(t)/log t dt) = 0.641, 0.748, 0.903, 0.963, 0.976, 1.005 at R = 1e3..1e8: the object IS the smoothed integral of M

lanes.caveats: The Omega(R^(3/2-eps)) statement for the integral of M is the explicit-formula consequence under RH with simple zeros; the numerics are what pin the constant and the exponent in the computed range. No Lean build was available in the closing session, so nothing here is machine checked.

variants_covered.native_moebius_atom_population: The RH_Lean #305 square-shell reformulation writes Matched_R = sum_{m in U_R} mu(m) over an explicit geometric atom set, with U_R = region1 (born-smooth, q<=c) union region3 (high, q>R), and proposes the balance |Matched_R|^2 <<_eps R^eps D_R with D_R = #squarefree in U_R <= R^2-1. That coordinate is a genuine improvement - it carries the native Moebius weight mu(cq) = -mu(c) with no pi-Li centering anywhere, so it is free of the Route B contamination - but the OBJECT is this lane's object, and the proposed balance is REFUTED AS A VIABLE RH ROUTE AND NUMERICALLY CONTRADICTED - not formally proved false. The repository proves the exact collapse matched = M(R^2-1) - positiveSmooth but proves NO lower bound or asymptotic estimate for positiveSmooth; a proof of the observed R^(3/2)/log R lower law would upgrade this to a theorem-level incompatibility. D_R <= R^2 makes the balance equivalent to |Matched_R| << R^(1+eps); combined with the verified identity matched = M(R^2-1) - positiveSmooth and the measured positiveSmooth ~ R^(3/2)/log R, it forces |M(R^2-1)| = Omega(X^(3/4-eps)) and therefore disproves RH. U_R is defined by excluding region2, and region2 IS positiveSmooth - the monotone pi-weighted Mertens sum carrying the X^(3/4) pathology. Encouraging numerics on this variant (dyadic max |Matched|^2/D_R decreasing: 1.259, 1.037, 0.690, 0.606, 0.786 for R up to 3162) are pre-asymptotic; using measured positiveSmooth and D_R ~ 0.6R^2 the ratio is about 1.7 at R=1e6, 74 at R=1e8 and 599 at R=5.37e8. The exact lifetime interval cq < R^2 <= 2cq with L(c,q)=max(c+1,floor(sqrt(cq))+1), U(c,q)=min(q-1,floor(sqrt(2cq))) and its LifetimeOverlapKernel pairing remain sound and reusable; only the diagonal balance is refuted.
variants_covered.scalar_cofactor_covariance: Collapsing each fibre to P_R(c) before the q-sum gives a rank-one Gram and creates no geometry. Correctly rejected upstream.
variants_covered.direct_falsifier: Run independently upstream and decisive without any modelling. Since D_R <= R^2, |Matched_R|^2/D_R >= (|Matched_R|/R)^2, so the ratio is bounded below with no need for D_R ~ 0.6R^2 and no assumption that matched ~ -positiveSmooth. Exact values via a Moebius prefix sieve plus memoised quotient recursion for M(R^2-1), with positiveSmooth from -sum_{q<=R prime} M(q-1): R=1e5 M=-33722 pos=42115 matched=-75837 ratio>=0.5751; R=2e5 M=-25295 pos=-41308 matched=16013 ratio>=0.0064; R=4e5 M=40748 pos=279029 matched=-238281 ratio>=0.3549; R=630957 M=133700 pos=719745 matched=-586045 ratio>=0.8627; R=8e5 M=104431 pos=-568654 matched=673085 ratio>=0.7079; R=1e6 M=62366 pos=1007875 matched=-945509 ratio>=0.8940. The last two exceed the ~0.786 late dyadic maximum observed for R<=3162, so the apparent downward trend has directly turned upward. R=1e6 was reproduced with a different summatory-Moebius cutoff giving the same three integers; positiveSmooth at R=1e5 and 1e6 matches the independent sweep in scripts/probes/posSmooth_1e9.py exactly.

lanes.what_would_reopen: Nothing at the level of the (bornSmooth, transport) pair or its far-upper survivor rewriting, since the obstruction is a lower bound on an object both forms contain. A split of the smooth mass whose uncancelled region is NOT a monotone-weighted Mertens sum would be a different lane. The invariant that has predicted every closure recorded here: a decomposition survives only if no piece is a monotone-weighted Moebius sum.

lanes.title: Attack the signed combined object C^PNT - 2 E^rec as a route to the H_{k,n} bound
lanes.claim: The PNT-centered coordinates expose favourable signed structure, so attacking C - 2E directly is progress on H_{k,n}.
lanes.obstruction: C - 2E is H_{k,n} by construction, not a new object. The centering operator Z is linear and M = (allPlus - 2*Bulk) - 2*Err, so Z[M] = Z[allPlus - 2 Bulk] - 2 Z[Err] = C - 2E identically; the repository's own theorem primorialMinimalSquareWheelNonzeroResponse_eq_mertensCenter already gives H = Z[M]. Hence C = H + 2E is an identity, and the pair of obligations {|C| << s, |E| << s} is EQUIVALENT to {|H| << s, |E| << s}, which is strictly stronger than the target {|H| << s}. The coordinate change therefore cannot reduce the difficulty; it can only relocate it. The observed C/E correlation reported as favourable is forced by that identity rather than being independent evidence: with C = H + 2E and |H| comparable to |2E|, positive correlation of C with E is automatic.

measured.identity_check: C - 2E = M(x) reproduced to floating tolerance at every x on a 240-point log grid from 1e4 to 1e8
measured.correlations: corr(C, 2E) = +0.8809, corr(M, 2E) = -0.9544, corr(C, M) = -0.6994 over the grid
measured.no_reduction: |C|/|M| has median 1.296 and only 34.6 percent of grid points have |C| < |M|; max|C|/sqrt(x) = 0.4095 against max|M|/sqrt(x) = 0.4045. Neither piece is systematically smaller than the target.

lanes.caveats: This closes the coordinate change as a REDUCTION, not the reciprocal-interval representation of E^rec, which is a genuine object and is recorded as still open under not_closed below.
lanes.what_would_reopen: An independent bound on the PNT-corrected comb C that does not route through M - i.e. combinatorial control of allPlus - 2*Bulk proved without assuming the Mertens bound. That would make the split a real reduction rather than a relabelling.

lanes.title: Divisor-band cancellation of the prime-by-prime correction (all-minus-one start, corrected prime by prime, bands d = floor(x/q))
lanes.claim: Starting every site at -1 and correcting prime by prime, the bands d = floor(x/q) cancel against each other, so the divisor-band structure supplies the cancellation for free and yields the Mertens bound.
lanes.obstruction: The band bulk does reindex onto the harmonic Moebius sum, but ONLY up to a finite boundary term, and that boundary is the whole difficulty. With S_D = sum_{d<=D} M(d)/(d(d+1)) and A_D = sum_{n<=D} mu(n)/n, finite Abel summation over the telescoping 1/d - 1/(d+1) gives S_D = sum_{n<=D} mu(n)(1/n - 1/(D+1)), i.e. the EXACT identity S_D = A_D - M(D)/(D+1). The formal infinite calculation sum_{d>=1} M(d)/(d(d+1)) = sum_{n>=1} mu(n)/n = 0 silently discards M(D)/(D+1); making that boundary vanish is already PNT-strength. Worse at the target rate: requiring A_D = O(D^(-1/2+eps)) forces M(D)/(D+1) = O(D^(-1/2+eps)), i.e. M(D) = O(D^(1/2+eps)) - the boundary term literally regenerates the original Mertens problem. So the mechanism transforms the problem into 'weighted band bulk = harmonic Moebius sum + Mertens boundary' rather than solving any part of it.
lanes.unification: This is the SAME 1/log^2 lane as the added-prime Euler-density ceiling recorded under not_closed. Both arrive at 1/log^2 from opposite directions: the added-prime lever because alpha_q ~ 1.2/q in the tail sums to log log Q, and the divisor bands because the zeroth-order band cancellation is exactly sum mu(n)/n, which is PNT and no more. Divisor-band cancellation and Euler-density cancellation are one lane, not two.

measured.identity_exact: S_D = A_D - M(D)/(D+1) verified in exact rational arithmetic for EVERY D = 1..3000, zero mismatches
measured.table: A_D - S_D equals M(D)/(D+1) to all printed digits at D = 10, 1e2, 1e3, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6, 1e7
measured.band_weights: band d has weight M(d) and population pi(I_d) ~ x/(d(d+1)log(x/d)); the d=2 band (q in (x/3,x/2]) contributes exactly zero since M(2)=0, and d=1 (q > x/2) needs no correction at all
measured.extra_band_cancellation: |S_D| decays faster than |A_D| (2.18e-6 against 1.02e-4 at D=1e7) because A_D ~ M(D)/(D+1) to within a few percent and S_D is the residue between them. Suggestive of genuine additional cancellation in the band coordinate, but it is a difference of two nearly equal quantities over only four decades - not a claim.

lanes.caveats: The next-order heuristic T ~ -x/log^2 x, obtained by expanding 1/log(x/d) and inserting sum mu(n) log n / n = -1, gives the right sign and magnitude (measured T = -3.56e5 against -x/log^2 x = -2.95e5 at x = 1e8) but is NOT established as a uniform asymptotic here: promoting it requires controlling the truncation and the weighted Moebius remainder, not merely substituting the formal identity. Treat it as a heuristic only.
lanes.what_would_reopen: Control of the Mertens boundary M(D)/(D+1) at rate D^(-1/2+eps) obtained independently of the Mertens bound itself. Absent that, the reindexing is an exact restatement.

not_closed.note: Recorded so the distinction is not lost. The added-prime contraction is real but its unweighted form has a ceiling: the observed per-prime ratios are exactly (p-1)/(p+1), the pure density factor, with no arithmetic gain, and prod_p (p-1)/(p+1) decays like 1/log^2 rather than like a power. In the k=20..40 band the residual runs up to 1.88x WORSE than independent behaviour. This constrains the mechanism to the centered object H_{k,n} rather than raw partial Moebius; it does not close a lane.

reciprocal_d_family.status: open, and the measured mechanism is now identified
reciprocal_d_family.note: The reciprocal-interval family E^rec = sum_d M(d) * (pi(I_d) - LiMass(I_d)) over the D = floor(x/y) ~ sqrt(x) fibres does exhibit square-root cancellation across d, and that cancellation is exactly what carries the termwise bound down to the target. Measured on a 240-point log grid to x = 1e8: sum_d |E_d| grows with exponent 0.678 (sub-range fits 0.635, 0.648, 0.706, 0.677 - robustly ABOVE the 0.5 target, so termwise absolute values cannot close, confirming CURRENT_PROOF_ROUTE section 6), while the signed |E^rec| fits exponent 0.51 and tracks sum_d|E_d|/sqrt(D) with median ratio 1.428 and log-log correlation 0.777. The median saving over the triangle bound is 24.9x at these scales, against a required saving of about x^0.18. So the answer to 'why does the combined signed operator save roughly X^(1/2)' is: square-root cancellation over the d-fibres, with essentially no margin. What this does NOT do is move the target, for the reason recorded in lane pnt-reciprocal-coordinate-change.

full_prefix_shell_lifetime_covariance.status: OPEN - the one genuinely open object coming out of the 2026-08-10 session. Start here.
full_prefix_shell_lifetime_covariance.object: Full-prefix smooth-tail plus dyadic-shell lifetime covariance. With X_R = R^2-1, q = P+(m), c = m/q (q=c=1 at m=1), b(m) = floor(sqrt m)+1, u(m) = min(q-1, floor(sqrt(2m))), s(m) = max(q, b(m)), give m the stage-membership set A(m) = [b(m),u(m)] u [s(m),inf) when c is odd, and [s(m),inf) when c is even, the finite interval empty when b(m) > u(m). The pieces are disjoint since u <= q-1 < s. The tail is ordinary smooth membership (m <= X_R and P+(m) <= R); the finite interval is the p=2 compressed transport shell (cq <= X_R < 2cq, q > R), whose atom carries its native weight mu(m) = mu(cq) = -mu(c) once transport is subtracted. Then M(R^2-1) = sum_m mu(m) * 1{R in A(m)}, with positiveSmooth NEVER split off.
full_prefix_shell_lifetime_covariance.gram: For W = [N, N+H) with 1 <= H <= N, K_W(m,n) = #(A(m) n A(n) n W) gives exactly sum_{R in W} |M(X_R)|^2 = sum_{m,n} mu(m)mu(n) K_W(m,n). No Cauchy step, no separated monotone-weighted component. Diagonal D_W = sum_m mu(m)^2 K_W(m,m) <= sum_{R in W} (R^2-1) <= 4HN^2, so the analytic target is sum_{m,n} mu(m)mu(n)K_W(m,n) <= C_eps N^eps D_W, yielding sum_{R in W}|M(X_R)|^2 << H N^(2+eps).
full_prefix_shell_lifetime_covariance.why_it_passes_the_gate: Region 2 is never separated: its persistent tails stay inside the same Gram as the finite shell lifetimes, so the monotone-weight gate does not fire on the coordinate. And the target is correctly scaled - at H=1 it is exactly pointwise RH-scale for M(X_R), which is TRUE under RH. That is what distinguishes it from the refuted native-Moebius atom balance, whose analogue was false because Matched ~ R^(3/2).
full_prefix_shell_lifetime_covariance.honest_status: It is RH restated in Gram coordinates, not a reduction. The diagonal bound is trivial and the inequality is square-root cancellation in a quadratic form. Its value rests entirely on whether the explicit interval-intersection structure of K_W gives leverage the flat statement does not. Unproven, but not foreclosed - which is more than any other lane reached.
first_two_tests: 1. DOUBLING TELESCOPE AND ATOM IDENTITY. The identity needs the high region {m <= X_R : P+(m) > R} to collapse onto the odd-c shell via mu(2c'q) = -mu(c'q); RHLean/Arithmetic/MoebiusDoubling should already carry it. Prove or numerically verify it together with the full atom identity M(R^2-1) = sum_m mu(m)1{R in A(m)}.
2. CONFIRM AMPLITUDES explicitly: tail amplitude = A_R and shell amplitude = -T_R.
3. Push scale probes through N >= 1e6, but treat E_TT, E_TS, E_SS as DIAGNOSTICS ONLY - by the amplitude collapse above they carry no independent information.

4. BEFORE ATTEMPTING ANY INEQUALITY, simplify the actual kernels. If a kernel collapses to a one-dimensional weighted Mertens object, that block closes. Fubini already collapses all three at the summed level, so the only live question is spectral, and only for K^SS.
5. Only then ask whether the interval geometry constrains the off-diagonal quadratic form beyond Fubini.
full_prefix_shell_lifetime_covariance.sizing: Any window test stopping short of N ~ 1e6 cannot distinguish this from the refuted lane; the earlier turn came at R ~ 5e5 to 1e6.
full_prefix_shell_lifetime_covariance.amplitude_collapse: CRITICAL NARROWING. Once the dyadic doubling telescope identifies the shell with the high-sector contribution, the stagewise split is still F_R = tail_R + shell_R = A_R - T_R = M(X_R), with tail amplitude = A_R and shell amplitude = -T_R. Hence at the scalar-amplitude level E_TT = sum A_R^2, 2E_TS = -2 sum A_R T_R, E_SS = sum T_R^2. Moreover ALL THREE Gram blocks collapse to those scalars by FUBINI ALONE - E_XY = sum_{m,n} mu(m)mu(n)#(A_X(m) n A_Y(n) n W) = sum_{R in W} X_R Y_R - so there is no two-dimensional structure anywhere at the level of the summed energy. The block cancellation is therefore NOT new structure; it is exact repackaging of the already-known A-versus-T near-cancellation.
full_prefix_shell_lifetime_covariance.what_the_gram_can_still_buy: The lane earns its keep only if the kernel is used WITHOUT RE-SUMMING: i.e. by bounding the quadratic form sum mu mu K spectrally (eigenvalues of K against sum mu^2) rather than by Fubini. Rank note for that route: tail atoms are half-lines [s(m), inf) fixed by the single scalar s(m), and {m : s(m) <= R} = {m <= X_R : P+(m) <= R} so sum_{s(m)<=R} mu(m) = A_R. K^TT and the tail side of K^TS are therefore rank-limited and their spectral bounds should be near-trivial. K^SS = |[b(m),u(m)] n [b(n),u(n)] n W| is a genuine two-interval intersection with richer spectrum. So the sharp open question is NOT 'does the kernel have 2D structure' but: does any spectral bound on K^SS beat what Fubini already gives?
full_prefix_shell_lifetime_covariance.constraint_on_any_shell_estimate: E_SS = sum T_R^2 is LARGE (T ~ X/log^2 X), so genuine structure in K^SS cannot be used to bound E_SS itself. It would have to exhibit E_SS's cancellation AGAINST E_TT and 2E_TS - i.e. survive recombination with two blocks that have already collapsed to scalars. That is a severe constraint on what a shell-shell estimate could look like, and it should be stated before anyone builds toward one.

primorial_block_two_sided_excursion.status: DEMOTED to a null-model fact on 2026-08-10. Needs no wheel explanation unless further evidence appears.
primorial_block_two_sided_excursion.original_claim: Every sufficiently large primorial block (W_k, W_{k+1}] carries a genuine two-sided interior excursion of R_k(x) = M(x) - M(W_k): L_k < 0 < U_k, and in the stronger form an interior overshoot U_k > max(0, R_k(W_{k+1})) and L_k < min(0, R_k(W_{k+1})) - a genuine hump and valley rather than a drift.
primorial_block_two_sided_excursion.wheel_measurement: Confirmed for every computable block. Holds for k = 3..8 (blocks (30,210] through (9699690,223092870]), fails for k = 0,1,2, so the startup index is 3 - one block EARLIER than the k_0=4 guessed from the figure. scripts/probes/excursion.py.
primorial_block_two_sided_excursion.why_demoted: A matched-null control settles it. Keeping the exact block length L_k = W_{k+1} - W_k but replacing the primorial start W_k by 100 deterministic pseudo-random starts a < W_k (so the endpoint sits just below W_{k+1}, preserving length and endpoint scale while destroying primorial alignment) gives: ALL 600 control intervals two-sided; 585 of 600 with the strong overshoot, and every sampled control satisfying it from k=4 onward. The wheel amplitudes max(U,-L)/sqrt(L_k) = 0.373, 0.327, 0.426, 0.395, 0.358, 0.445 land at the 53rd, 45th, 61st, 77th, 25th and 79th percentiles of their matched-control distributions - completely ordinary. The control implementation reproduces the wheel U_k, L_k, R(end) values exactly, so the two implementations agree.
primorial_block_two_sided_excursion.consistent_with_null: For a long approximately zero-drift signed walk, failing to visit one side of the starting level, or ending exactly at the running max or min, both become exceptional as length grows. So a long path generically produces an interior hump and valley. That is only a heuristic for Moebius, but the controls show the primorial boundary is not supplying the effect. The observed startup at k=3 tracks INTERVAL LENGTH, not the arrival of a wheel mechanism: at k=2 (length 24) most same-length starts stay one-sided, while by k=3 (length 180) all 100 controls are already two-sided though only 85 percent have the strong overshoot.
ruled_out_as_wheel_signatures: raw excursion amplitude (the 0.31-0.44 band is generic)
fixed peak/trough orientation - the wheel data itself alternates, peak first for k=3,4,5,7 but not k=6,8
primorial_block_two_sided_excursion.reframed_question: What feature of the Mertens trajectory inside a primorial block IS statistically different from matched non-primorial intervals? Remaining candidates, all more discriminating: the square-block identity of the winning extremum (r+- were (9,14),(37,40),(138,155),(680,596),(2545,2666),(14841,13413)); its relation to the wheel's Fourier response; correlations of successive square-block increments within the interval; or an arithmetic signature tied specifically to W_k.
primorial_block_two_sided_excursion.scarcity_caveat: Primorial blocks grow superexponentially: block 9 ends at 6.5e9, block 10 at 2.0e11. Six non-startup blocks is essentially the entire obtainable dataset, not a first sample. Any wheel-side conjecture inherits this - it can never acquire the four-decade support that closed the positiveSmooth lane.

multiarm_prime_field_coherence.experiment: Prime arms added successively from 2 to the sqrt(U) cutoff on three complete primorial blocks (2310,30030], (30030,510510], (510510,9699690]. At the final cutoff the corrected field matched mu(n) at every site in all three blocks, so this is an exact finite implementation of the wheel construction.
multiarm_prime_field_coherence.result_1_raw_product_fails: Even with ALL prime arms through sqrt(U) present, the centered RAW product has essentially no path correlation with the Mertens residual: -0.038, 0.111, -0.151 for k=5,6,7, with normalized excursion 5.81, 14.72, 42.26. Prime-arm interference alone is not the Mertens walk; the smooth-core orientation correction is indispensable. (Consistent with what the repo already asserts - the corrected wheel is the object, not the raw comb.)
multiarm_prime_field_coherence.result_2_sitewise_is_the_wrong_metric: THE USEFUL FINDING. On block k=7, cutoff p<=1619 already gets 99.46 percent of individual sites right, yet path correlation is only 0.206 and the excursion is 23.37/sqrt(U) against a true 0.348 - about 67x too large. At p<=2557, only 0.055 percent of sites remain wrong and the excursion is still 9x the final one. So corr(partial field, mu) > 0.999 is compatible with a materially wrong cumulative path: the Mertens trajectory depends on the ZERO-FREQUENCY BIAS of the error set E_y(x) = sum_{n<=x}(mu(n) - F_y(n)), not on its size. Extrema also lock in very late - on k=7 the trough sits at phase 0.958 with 568 wrong sites and only moves to the correct 0.718 at 181 wrong sites; on k=6 the peak does not settle until six erroneous sites remain.
multiarm_prime_field_coherence.result_3_coherence_NEEDS_A_CONTROL: Reported as the headline: at cutoff 2903 on block k=7, 568 wrong sites out of 9189180 (0.0062 percent) shift the endpoint by 1113 (partial -810 against true 303). Similarly on k=6, 61 wrong sites shift by 115. ARITHMETIC CHECK: since mu(n), F(n) in {-1,0,1}, each site contributes at most 2, so the maximum possible shift from 568 sites is 1136 - the measured 1113 is 98 percent of maximum, against ~sqrt(568) = 24 for random signs. That is TOO close to maximal to be a subtle arithmetic conspiracy, and is the signature of a DEFINITIONAL constraint. Before treating this as a discovery, check whether the residual error set is sign-homogeneous BY CONSTRUCTION: print the sign distribution of mu(n) - F_y(n) over those 568 sites. All one sign => the coherence is a property of the wheel construction, not a fact about high primes. Mixed signs still summing to 1113 => genuine.
multiarm_prime_field_coherence.gate_note: The proposed reframing 'why do the high-prime correction shells have coherent signed mass, and why does their full completion leave only sqrt(X)-scale residue' has two clauses. The SECOND is the RH target restated, so rule 1 applies to it. Only the first clause is live, and the sign-homogeneity control decides it.
multiarm_prime_field_coherence.control_outcome: Sign distribution of mu(n) - F_y(n) at k=7, y=2903: +2 on 545 sites, +1 on 23 sites, -1 and -2 on none. So 545*2 + 23 = 1113 is 100 percent of the ATTAINABLE signed mass, not 98 percent of the naive 2*568 = 1136 ceiling, which was unattainable because 23 errors have magnitude 1. Same explanation at k=6, y=659: 54 semiprime errors * 2 + 7 square errors * 1 = 115, exactly the endpoint correction from -156 to -41.
multiarm_prime_field_coherence.theorem: Let U be the fixed upper endpoint and suppose 2y^2 > U. Then for every n <= U the partial corrected field has error exactly: mu(n) - F_y(n) = 2 if n = qr with y < q < r both prime; = 1 if n = q^2 with q > y prime; = 0 otherwise. Proof sketch: a selected prime square kills both mu and the partial comb. One unresolved prime q > y contributes precisely the parity flip that makes the provisional field already agree with mu, so a mismatch needs at least TWO unresolved prime factors. But then n >= qr > y^2 > U/2, and any extra cofactor c >= 2 gives cqr > 2y^2 > U. So the only survivors are n = qr and n = q^2, and in both the partial field assigns -1 while mu is +1 and 0 respectively. Every error is therefore POSITIVE and the late shell is forced to be one-signed.
multiarm_prime_field_coherence.threshold_confirmed: For k=7 the threshold is sqrt(U/2) = 2202.24. Below it the signs are genuinely mixed - at y=1619 the distribution is (-2:6364, -1:93, +1:187, +2:42837) with signed/absolute = 0.740, and at y=1987 it is (-2:868, -1:27, +1:143, +2:23653) with 0.928. The first tested cutoff above the threshold is 2357, and coherence is exactly 1.000 there and at every larger cutoff (2557, 2741, 2903, 2999, 3037). The onset of perfect coherence lands precisely where the size argument says the unresolved factorization type collapses to semiprimes and prime squares.
multiarm_prime_field_coherence.what_survives: Only the metric finding, now with a clean explanation: SITEWISE AGREEMENT IS A CATASTROPHICALLY WEAK METRIC FOR PREFIX AGREEMENT, because a tiny exceptional set can be sign-homogeneous for an elementary factorization reason. In the late regime the path error is not mysterious at all - it is a positive prime-pair counting function, E_y(U) = 2*#{qr in (L,U] : q,r > y, q != r} + #{q^2 in (L,U] : q > y}. Separated, that is exactly the large monotone object rules 1 and 2 warn against, so its role is EXPLANATORY, not a cancellation mechanism. Do not build an analytic route on it.
multiarm_prime_field_coherence.remaining_live_question: Below the threshold, y < sqrt(U/2), the error distribution genuinely carries both signs. Is its cumulative behaviour explainable by CRT phase mixing? That is where a dynamics analogy still has something nontrivial to say. CAUTION: coherence degrades only gracefully below the threshold - 0.928 at y=1987 and still 0.740 at y=1619 - so a dominant sign persists well into the 'mixed' regime. Any test for genuine phase mixing needs y far below sqrt(U/2), not just below it.

gate.rule_1_monotone_weight: Before formalizing a decomposition, reindex every separated piece. If any piece becomes a one-dimensional monotone-weighted Moebius prefix, a reciprocal Mertens transform, or a PNT discrepancy, reject the split before attempting a bound.
gate.rule_2_scale: Reject any transformation that turns the full Mertens object into separately estimated pieces whose observed or exact natural scales exceed the RH target - even if neither piece visibly Abel-collapses to a monotone Moebius sum.
gate.coverage: Rule 1 catches the disguised closures: canonical-orientation-split (piece = pi-weighted Mertens sum), pnt-reciprocal-coordinate-change (piece = PNT discrepancy, C = H + 2E), divisor-band-harmonic-mobius (piece = harmonic Moebius sum with Mertens boundary), blockwise-delta-triangle-sum (absolute values destroy the telescoping), and the native-Moebius atom balance. Rule 2 catches A_R and T_R immediately, which rule 1 does not: neither Abel-collapses, but both are intrinsically of size X/log^2 X. Together: every useful decomposition must PRESERVE the cancellation between the two individually large square-root sectors. Rule 3 caught the primorial two-sided-excursion phenomenon immediately: it is generic to intervals of that length, not a wheel effect. Rule 4 caught the multi-arm coherence: 1113 from 568 sites looked like emergent alignment and was forced by an elementary factorization argument.
gate.forbidden_isolations: A_R (square-root smooth mass), T_R (transport), positiveSmooth_R. The first two are intrinsically large and nearly cancel; the third carries the X^(3/4) pathology.
gate.logical_status: The two rules have DIFFERENT logical status and must not be applied alike. Rule 1 is STRUCTURAL: if exact algebra exposes a monotone-weighted Moebius sum, a reciprocal Mertens transform, or an isolated PNT discrepancy, the route is closed BY INSPECTION, no probe needed. Rule 2 is a MAGNITUDE SCREEN: unless the natural scale is proved, it is an EMPIRICAL VETO requiring a probe, and it therefore costs a run rather than an inspection. Accordingly the A_R ~ X/log^2 X diagnosis is labelled MEASURED AND STRONGLY SUGGESTED, not theorem-level: it rests on three points over two decades matched against the X/log^2 X heuristic, and is NOT backed by the four-decade evidence behind the positiveSmooth law.
gate.rule_3_wheel_specificity: Before attributing any observed block phenomenon to the prime wheel, compare it against same-length, same-endpoint-scale intervals with the primorial alignment destroyed. This is a NULL-CONTROL gate and it is cheap. It is doubly important on the wheel side because only ~log log x primorial blocks exist below x - matched controls are one of the few ways to generate enough counterfactual data to separate structure from appearance.
gate.rule_4_definitional_maximum: When an empirical effect lies near its algebraic maximum, classify the support and the allowed per-site contributions BEFORE attributing the effect to arithmetic correlation or dynamics. Earned 2026-08-10: it would have closed the 'coherent high-prime shell' interpretation immediately, without a run.

scales.measured_separation: A_R and T_R are each ~ X/log^2 X while M(X) = A_R - T_R is ~ sqrt(X). Measured |A_R| = 124, 6355, 354099 at R = 100, 1000, 10000, i.e. |A_R|/sqrt(X) = 1.24, 6.36, 35.4 - diverging like sqrt(X)/log^2 X. At X=1e8, A_R = -354099 against a target of 1e4 and against -1.2 X/log^2 X = -354000. So RH-scale control of A or T individually is structurally mis-scaled, and the near-cancellation between them is the entire content of M.
scales.wheel_cutoff_correction: CORRECTION recorded 2026-08-10. It is wrong to infer from Q_k > 6U_k that the wheel's prime coordinates reach only log U_k. That conflates two different prime scales. The prime defining the primorial BLOCK ENDPOINT is logarithmic in that endpoint, but the WHEEL deliberately extends its prime coordinates to the square-root cutoff: RHLean/Arithmetic/PrimorialWheelScale.lean defines primorialWheelCutoff k = Nat.sqrt (primorialBlockUpper k) with 'every prime coordinate at most the square-root cutoff', and the square-sensitive modulus is Q_k = prod_{p <= sqrt(U_k)} p^2. Consequently the wheel-smooth population is NOT the very thin log-x-smooth population; near the top of a synchronized block its cutoff is exactly the same square-root scale appearing in A_R, so the wheel smooth sector runs into the SAME large-smooth-mass obstruction just measured for A_R rather than offering a thin-set escape.
scales.periodicity_still_dead: Q_k > 6U_k does still kill the periodicity idea: no complete wheel period fits inside the arithmetic block. The quantitative bridge uses the large modulus to make the zero-frequency coupling contractive (rho < 1/6), not to supply many periods for averaging.
